plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like flowers. It thrives in mild, humid climates and is a classic winter bloomer in gardens, with thousands of cultivars in single, semi-double, and fully double forms.
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and China; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Western Europe, Australia, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative, produces the leaves used to make all true tea, and Camellia japonica seed oil has been used in Japan for hair care and cooking.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A low-growing perennial with nodding, cup-shaped white flowers that often age to pinkish tones, with bright yellow stamens. It can bloom through snow and frost in shady woodland gardens.
plants.location: Native to the mountains of central and southern Europe; cultivated in temperate gardens across Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Despite its name it is not a true rose, and all parts of the plant are toxic. Its flowers are protected from cold by the plant's natural antifreeze-like cell chemistry and sturdy leathery foliage.

plants.name: Hippeastrum puniceum
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with large trumpet-shaped flowers on tall hollow stalks. Hybrids derived from Hippeastrum species are popular winter-flowering houseplants in the Northern Hemisphere, while in the Southern Hemisphere and tropics they bloom in the warm season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter indoors in the Northern Hemisphere; summer in parts of South America and the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to tropical and subtropical Central and South America and the Caribbean; grown worldwide
plants.funFact: Hippeastrum bulbs can reach the size of a grapefruit and can flower again for many years if given a dormant rest period.

plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree whose fragrant blossoms appear on bare branches in late winter, often before the leaves. It is a beloved symbol of perseverance and is prized in gardens and bonsai.
plants.location: Native to southern China; cultivated in Japan, Korea, Taiwan, and mild regions of the United States and Europe
plants.funFact: In East Asian art it is one of the 'Three Friends of Winter' along with pine and bamboo because it blossoms in the cold.
